story_of_day.headline: Oil crashes 9% as Washington blames the Iran war for its rout
story_of_day.story: Trump said "it's the gasoline price" that cost Republicans Congress, and Vice President Vance said the war was the reason for the losses. Traders took that as a sign Washington wants out. Brent fell about 9% to roughly $94.7, its lowest since early September and far below the near-$118 of last Friday. Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted "no to war".
story_of_day.so_what: The war has become a political cost for the White House, which raises the odds of a deal. But Iran still says Hormuz stays shut, so the price is betting on a settlement that has not happened.

last_time.text: Last run Brent was about $101.6 and four tankers had been hit by mines near Hormuz. It is now $94.6, a drop of about 7% in half a day.

story_of_day.money_angle: Brent $94.63, WTI $88.04. The S&P 500 is at 7,689 and the dollar index slipped to 101.5.

cards.headline: Markets cheer a checked Trump
cards.story: US stocks surged after the Democratic sweep: the Dow rose close to 3%, its best day in over a year, and the dollar slid. Investors are betting that a Congress run by Democrats will rein in Trump's erratic policymaking. Mississippi and Alaska Senate races are still too close to call.
cards.so_what: Analysts warn a lame-duck president could still be unpredictable on tariffs and foreign policy, where Congress has less say.

last_time.text: Last run Democrats had just won both chambers. Today's news is the market reaction and a few remaining races.

cards.money_angle: S&P 500 is 7,689, up from 7,569 at the last run. AUD/USD is 0.7007.

cards.headline: Dhaka squeezed by wage riots and a gas shortage
cards.story: Clashes during garment protests injured 50 people and shut about 200 factories, with workers demanding a Tk30,000 minimum wage. Separately, gas supply to power plants was cut to manage an LNG shortage, which cost 1,100MW of gas-fired power. Demand was still fully met on Wednesday afternoon.
cards.so_what: Asian LNG has tripled since January on the Iran war, so Bangladesh's wage fight and its energy bill are the same squeeze. Falling oil may ease it, but gas stays tight.

last_time.text: Last run the wage board had started talks and 529 factories were disrupted. Protests continue, and the LNG shortage is new.

cards.headline: Ukraine school strike toll hits 40
cards.story: Zelensky says 40 are now confirmed dead after the Russian strike on a school in Komyshuvakha, with dozens possibly still under rubble. Ukraine says bodycam video shows a deadly double-tap bombing. The Kremlin says it hopes the US vote won't disturb Trump's "peacemaking efforts".
cards.so_what: Moscow is betting a weakened Trump still wants a deal on its terms. Europe is meeting the US in Brussels on support for Ukraine.

last_time.text: Last run the Kremlin was already hoping the midterms would not change talks. The toll from the Komyshuvakha strike has since risen.

cards.headline: Israel's deadlock meets a colder Washington
cards.story: Israel's president Herzog has begun talks with parties after the election left no clear majority, warning that "not every promise can be fulfilled" if they want to avoid another vote. The Guardian argues the US midterms were a rebuke of the US-Israel relationship, after Trump floated ending military aid.
cards.so_what: A new Democratic Congress holds the purse strings on that aid, and a divided Israeli government is weaker going into any Iran deal.

last_time.text: Earlier Trump said US aid to Israel ends this year, and Netanyahu's bloc was about eight seats short. Coalition talks have now formally started.

watch.title: Does Iran reopen Hormuz?
watch.text: Brent has priced in a deal. If Tehran keeps the Strait closed and talks stall, expect a sharp rebound.

takes_review.text: I said don't chase oil and flagged a close below $98 as the sign I was wrong. Brent was $105.92 then and is $94.63 now, so by my own test I was wrong: the market did pick a side, and it was down. Staying out of a one-way bet cost nothing, but I didn't see a drop this size coming.
I said wait for a pullback in renewables rather than chase the gap. The S&P 500 is up from 7,569 to 7,689 since, and I don't track renewables prices here, so it is too early to call. It stays open.
